question: In structural equation models estimated with small samples, how does Bayesian estimation compare with frequentist (maximum likelihood) estimation in terms of performance, accuracy, and bias?
source: SYNERGY dataset (asreview/synergy-dataset) Smid_2020; social-science methodology review 'Bayesian Versus Frequentist Estimation for Structural Equation Models in Small Sample Contexts' (Struct Equ Modeling 2020, doi:10.1080/10705511.2019.1577140); gold = label_included==1 rows with DOI, resolved via [AID]
notes: Created with make_fixture.py. No baseline strategy: use evals/generate.py (Phase 2). Harness reports reachable vs. unreachable gold separately.

version_change.reason: Initial evaluation protocol for the Bayesian-vs-frequentist SEM recall fixture.
version_change.decision_source: Evaluation fixture author; scope derived from Smid et al. 2020 (Struct Equ Modeling, doi:10.1080/10705511.2019.1577140).

review.question: In structural equation models estimated with small samples, how does Bayesian estimation compare with frequentist (maximum likelihood) estimation in terms of performance, accuracy, and bias?

framework.name: Methods-comparison (model x estimation method x sample context x evaluation)
framework.rationale: This is a methodological simulation-study review, not a clinical PICO question. The two axes that every eligible study shares and that drive retrieval are the model family (structural equation / latent-variable models) and the estimation method (Bayesian). The small-sample context, the simulation-study design, the frequentist comparator, and the social-science field are eligibility qualifiers that are inconsistently worded in abstracts, so they are screening-only to protect recall.

slots.label: Model family
slots.description: Structural equation / latent-variable model family (SEM, CFA, latent growth/class, multilevel, mediation).

slots.label: Estimation method
slots.description: Bayesian estimation (with priors / MCMC), the method under evaluation.

slots.label: Evaluation
slots.description: Simulation-study comparison of estimator performance against frequentist/maximum-likelihood methods.

inclusion.label: Structural-equation / latent-variable model
inclusion.description: The study concerns a structural equation model or a model in the SEM/latent-variable family (CFA, latent growth/class, multilevel, mediation).

inclusion.label: Evaluates Bayesian estimation
inclusion.description: The study investigates Bayesian estimation (with prior distributions / MCMC) of such a model.

inclusion.label: Compares against frequentist estimation
inclusion.description: Performance of Bayesian estimation is compared against frequentist / maximum-likelihood (or alternative) estimation.

inclusion.label: Small-sample context
inclusion.description: The estimation problem is set in a small-sample (or few-cluster) context.

inclusion.label: Simulation-based evaluation
inclusion.description: Estimator performance is evaluated via a Monte Carlo / simulation study (optionally alongside an empirical example).

inclusion.label: Peer-reviewed, social-science methodology
inclusion.description: A peer-reviewed methodological paper in the field of the social/behavioural sciences.

exclusion.label: Not a latent-variable/SEM model
exclusion.description: The model is not in the structural-equation / latent-variable family.

exclusion.label: No Bayesian estimation
exclusion.description: The study does not evaluate Bayesian estimation.

exclusion.label: No performance evaluation
exclusion.description: The study is a purely applied analysis with no simulation/performance comparison of estimators.

concepts.label: Structural equation / latent-variable model family
concepts.definition: The statistical model under study: structural equation models and the broader latent-variable family (confirmatory factor analysis, latent growth/class, multilevel, and mediation models). Retrieval must not depend on the single phrase 'structural equation'.
concepts.rationale: A shared essential concept: every eligible study estimates a model in this family. It needs broad synonym expansion because the family spans SEM, CFA, latent growth, multilevel, and mediation labels.

concepts.label: Bayesian estimation
concepts.definition: The estimation method under evaluation: Bayesian estimation using prior distributions and MCMC/Gibbs sampling. Distinct from the frequentist comparator, which is handled at screening.
concepts.rationale: A shared essential concept: every eligible study evaluates Bayesian estimation, so it co-anchors the search with the model family.

properties.label: Small-sample (or few-cluster) context
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that the estimation problem is set in a small-sample or few-cluster context. Do not add a small-sample AND block.
properties.recall_rationale: Small-sample phrasing ('small sample', 'few clusters', 'limited N', 'small data set') is inconsistent and often absent from abstracts; as a search block it drops eligible papers (empirically only ~11/14 of the gold).

properties.label: Simulation-based performance evaluation
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that estimator performance is evaluated via a Monte Carlo / simulation study. Do not add a simulation AND block.
properties.recall_rationale: Simulation-study terms are frequently not in the abstract of methods papers; as a block they bottleneck recall.

properties.label: Comparison against frequentist / maximum-likelihood estimation
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that Bayesian estimation is compared against frequentist / maximum-likelihood (or an alternative) estimator. Do not add a comparator AND block.
properties.recall_rationale: The comparator arm ('frequentist', 'maximum likelihood', 'WLSMV') is not always named in title/abstract; a comparator block would silently drop eligible comparisons.

properties.label: Peer-reviewed social-science methodology
properties.instructions: Confirm at screening that the paper is a peer-reviewed methodological paper in the social/behavioural sciences. Apply no field or publication-type search limit.
properties.recall_rationale: Field/discipline is essentially never stated in abstracts; a field limit would be a severe, arbitrary recall filter.

decisions.label: Methodological (study-design) filter
decisions.rationale: Recall-first evaluation build; the simulation-study design is confirmed at screening, not by a search-time hedge.

decisions.label: Database limits
decisions.rationale: No language, field, publication-status, or date limits are authorized for the evaluation build.

date_boundaries.rationale: No date boundaries; the evaluation scores against a fixed gold set and applies no date limit.

recall.policy: Recall first; decline the optional no-seed heuristic during evaluation because hidden gold is scored independently.

workload.policy: Do not narrow solely because retrieval is large.
workload.selection_rule: Workload may choose only among variants that meet the held-out recall requirement.

protocol_status: tightened; lock-validated and compiled. Achievable recall ~13/14 with a screenable 2-block scope (Bayesian estimation x SEM/latent-variable model family); the applied outlier PMID 25765534 lacks any SEM term in its abstract and is only reachable by generic terms that explode retrieval ~40x, so it is left outside the precise scope by design.
